action: Open the Animation menu tab.
Select the Joint Tool.
Click around the viewport to demonstrate how joints can be created in unwanted positions.
notes: The instructor demonstrates why using orthographic views is preferable.

action: Undo the incorrectly created joints.
notes: Clears the unwanted joints.

action: Switch to the orthographic views.
notes: Displays the front, side and other orthographic views.

action: Select the Side View and click to place the initial pelvis joint.
notes: Establishes the pelvis position.

action: Switch to the Front View and click to create the hip joint.
notes: Establishes the hip position.

action: Maximize the Side View.
Click and drag downward to position the knee joint.
Click to create and position the ankle joint.
Click to create the ball-of-foot joint.
Click to create the toe joint.
Press Enter to finish creating the joint chain.
notes: Finalizes the Joint Tool operation.

action: Return to the Perspective View to inspect the created joint chain.
Select the upper leg joint and rename it to Left Thigh.
notes: Establishes the naming convention for the left leg.

action: Use the Up and Down arrow keys to navigate between parent and child joints in the hierarchy.
notes: Up selects the parent; Down selects the child.

action: Select the child joint and rename it to Left Knee.
Select the next child joint and rename it to Left Ankle.
Select the next child joint and rename it to Left Toe.
Select the final child joint and rename it to Left Toe Tip.
Check that all joints have been named correctly using a consistent left-side prefix.
notes: The naming convention helps with mirroring.

action: Open the Mirror Joint tool settings.
Enter left in the Search For field.
Enter right in the Replace With field.
notes: Replaces the left-side prefix in mirrored joint names.

action: Click Apply to mirror the joints using the current axis settings.
notes: The instructor demonstrates the initial mirroring result.

action: Inspect the mirrored joints and identify that they are reflected across the wrong axis.
notes: The default XY reflection is not the desired result.

action: Undo the incorrectly mirrored joints.
notes: Removes the incorrect mirror operation.

action: Select the YZ mirror axis.
notes: Changes the reflection plane.

action: Click Mirror to mirror the joints across the YZ axis.
notes: Creates the joints on the opposite side in the intended position.

action: Use the Up and Down arrow keys to inspect the mirrored joint hierarchy and verify the names.
notes: Confirms that the mirrored joints have the correct right-side names.

action: Locate the IK Handle tool in the Animation tools.
Select the IK Handle tool to activate it.
Open the IK Handle tool settings by double-clicking its icon.
notes: Alternative to directly activating the tool.

action: Click Reset Tool to restore the IK Handle tool settings.
Open the Solver dropdown and inspect the default SC Solver selection.
notes: SC Solver is selected by default.

action: Change the solver from SC Solver to RP Solver.
notes: RP stands for Rotate Plane.

action: Select the thigh joint as the starting joint for the IK handle.
keys_or_menu: IK Handle Tool > Click Thigh Joint

action: Select the ankle joint as the ending joint for the IK handle.
keys_or_menu: IK Handle Tool > Click Ankle Joint
notes: Creates an IK handle between the thigh and ankle.

action: Inspect the generated IK handle and its associated rotation plane.
notes: The plane determines the direction in which the joints bend.

action: Compare the IK-controlled leg with the opposite leg, which still requires individual joint rotation.
notes: Explains the benefit of IK controls.

action: Select the newly created IK handle.
Activate the Transform/Move tool.
Move the IK handle to reposition the leg.
notes: The thigh and knee joints automatically adjust to the new position.

action: Observe how the thigh and knee joints adjust when the IK handle is moved.
notes: Demonstrates automatic joint positioning.

action: Observe how the IK handle can control the foot's ground-contact position during character movement.
notes: Explains the practical use of IK for walking animations.

action: Undo the recent IK handle movements to return the leg to its original position.
notes: Restores the leg to its initial position on the ground.

action: Prepare to configure the same Rotate Plane IK setup on the opposite leg.
notes: The instructor moves on to setting up the other side.

action: Begin setting up the Rotate Plane IK handle on the right leg.
notes: The transcript does not include the individual operations for this setup.
